feature: This Minute: Courteney & Jen’s Jewelry by Mary Margrill

Courteney & Jen’s Jewelry

How Tinseltown’s tight twosome are saying “I’ll be there for you”

“If we were lesbians, we would marry each other,” Jennifer Aniston, 36, has gushed about longtime pal—and new neighbor—Courteney Cox, 41. (Aniston recently acquired digs a mere 20 houses away from Cox and David Arquette’s home in Malibu.) Cox’s take on the godmother of her baby, Coco, 1? “The reason I love Jennifer so much is I feel safe with her.” To show their mutual devotion, the pair are now sporting 14-karat yellow-gold BEST FRIENDS pendants from NYC-based M² Design by Mary Margrill.

The token of their affection Just another best-friend necklace it ain’t. “I combine meaningful pieces with a classic timeless look,” designer Mary Margrill, 41, tells Us. “I [aim to] make jewelry that moves and inspires people.”

Golden girls Other A-listers who love M²’s simple designs? Jennifer Garner, Penelope Cruz and Kirsten Dunst have all taken a shine to Margrill’s Love Necklace (from $290, ylang-ylang.com).

Aniston keeps Cox close to her heart. ($325, ylang-ylang.com)

title: Women’s Wear Daily
feature: WWD Monday: Mary Margrill Couture Launch
body_html:
18-KARAT BABY: Jewelry designer Mary Margrill is upping the ante with a new 18-karat gold collection.

“It’s a whole new realm for me,” said the New York designer, whose signature is to stamp her pieces with words such as “Love” and “Blessed.” “We’re in a time where people are more introspective.”

The pieces are a bit more expensive than her other jewelry, at wholesale prices ranging from $250 to $4,000; one-of-a-kind pieces, like a gem-laden necklace, can climb to $10,000. M2 Design by Mary Margrill’s 14-karat gold line wholesales from $150 to $900 and is sold at stores such as Neiman Marcus and Ylang 23 in Dallas. The 18-karat line will make its debut at Couture in Las Vegas next month.

inner goddess

Mary Margrill could be considered as much a philosopher as a designer. “I discover new worlds of possibility,” says Margrill, who introduces her first 18k white and yellow gold jewelry this month. A devotee of history and spirituality, Margrill combines elements from yoga, numerology, and talismans from ancient cultures in Egypt, Asia, Tibet, and more. “I fuse them together to channel the one concept of feminine energy,” she says, pointing out an example like her cartouche pendant that combines symbols of the Egyptian goddess, Isis, Lakshmi, a Hindi goddess of abundance, and Venus, the Roman goddess of love. title: FrontDesk
feature: What’s Hot: Cool = M2 is Mary Margrill Couture
body_html:
Cool = M2

Lindsay and Demi love these gems with a spiritual message

Usually it takes designers years and years of struggling to make a name for themselves. But Mary Margrill, the New York designer behind the M2 line (pronounced M-squared), found that celebrities and socialites were snatching up her jewels within just months of her launch. Because her unique collection is based on spirituality, everyone from Uma Thurman and Halle Berry quickly fell in love with the baubles that host positive messages, such as her popular pendants that say, “I am Blessed,” or “I am Loved.”

“I believe we can take a lot of strength from words,” Margrill says. “They inspire you, and remind you of what’s really important everyday.” But that doesn’t mean the pieces are hokey. “This isn’t a crunchy granola thing,” she says of the line. “It’s all solid 14- and 18kt gold, with diamonds and precious stones. And the words are about inspiring people and making a difference in their lives when they put the necklaces on each morning. It’s reminding themselves, and everyone of their belief or their daily mantra.” And it’s not just a cutesy gimmick Margrill came up with to sell her wares. “Everything I do in my own life is spiritual—from yoga to writing to meditating every morning,” she says. “It’s how I live, and I truly believe in infusing positive energy into each piece.”

title: Neiman Marcus
feature: Designer Q&A: Mary Margrill Diamond Heart Charm Necklace
body_html:
Designer Q&A: Valentine’s Edition with M² Design by Mary Margrill

As an NM editor I see a wide selection of jewelry (not that I’m complaining, mind you!) but pieces from M² Design by Mary Margrill really stand out. I’m especially taken with the Diamond Heart Charm Necklace, which would make a PERFECT Valentine’s Day gift. It’s so romantic, I decided to ask its creator, Mary Margrill, about her Valentine’s Day favorites.

What are the best gifts to give and to receive on Valentine’s Day?
I always think the best gifts to give on Valentine’s Day are the ones that really connect to our hearts and souls. A unique and inspirational piece of jewelry with an extra special message makes a particularly meaningful impact and keeps that message alive forever. Even when Valentine’s Day has passed, I still love giving my pieces for this exact reason. As for gifts for me, since I can design pieces for myself...I love receiving flowers with a deeply thoughtful message that really resonates.

What’s the most romantic Valentine’s Day you’ve had?
Figure skating with the love of my life at midnight... at an outdoor skating rink in Paris...with all the beautiful lights illuminating from the trees while incredibly classic French bistro music plays in the background. So much romance in the air...hearts pounding and smiles everywhere...Ooh La La

title: The Record-Review
feature: Jewelry designer exhibits ‘One World’ necklace
body_html:
Jewelry designer exhibits ‘One World’ necklace

Mary Magrill, an artist, renowned jewelry designer, and philosopher based in Katonah whose work is steeped in spirituality, has accepted an invitation from the prestigious Minneapolis Institution of Arts to exhibit her diamond-encrusted “One World” necklace as part of the “Faith in Motion” gallery event. The handmade necklace unites symbols of seven world faiths in 14-karat white gold and 2 carat total weight of white diamonds. The defining character of this whimsical yet powerful piece is its peace-sign [illegible] lace is valued between $16,000 and $20,000 and is available for purchase upon request at www.marymargrill.com.

Documenting the small artifacts carried by explorers, merchants, colonists, pilgrims and missionaries as they carried their cultures and beliefs around the globe is the premise of “Faith in Motion.” Portable art played a major role in the spread of religions throughout the world.

The exhibit runs through July 31 at the Minneapolis Institute of Arts, 2400 3rd Ave. South in Min[illegible]

Mary Magrill, creator of the “One World Necklace.”
